properties.statement:
BL-198 ASKED FOR THIS MEASUREMENT AND IT HAS NOW BEEN TAKEN TWICE, IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS, ONE RELEASE APART. fact:bl-198 says: 'import_graph and the merge driver both compare property maps, so suppressing defaults changes what "changed" means to compare_designs and to merge=reflow2. That is the real cost of this row and it should be measured, not assumed.' The cost is now on the record from live data, and it is larger than byte bloat.

    2026-08-08   0.24.0 server vs 0.25.0 binary        108 phantom property findings
    2026-08-10   0.25.0-era committed file vs 0.27.0    95 phantom property findings

BOTH RUNS PRODUCED A CONFIDENT FALSE DEFECT CLAIM, BY DIFFERENT AGENTS, NEITHER HAVING READ THE OTHER. The 2026-08-08 session concluded export_graph silently deletes property values and that its divergence guard is blind to property-level loss, wrote that into a PR body and a handoff note, and retracted it after one probe (fact:correction-the-export-loses-nothing-the-108-were-serialized-defaults). On 2026-08-10 I made the same claim about the same guard on the same two properties, in the opposite direction, and it was found only because search_design surfaced the earlier retraction. A REPRODUCED MISREADING IS STRONGER EVIDENCE THAN A REPORTED ONE: the instrument is not merely noisy, it is reliably misleading to a competent reader, which is the property that matters for a tool meant to be run at orientation time.

THE DIRECTION FLIPPED, WHICH IS THE NEW PART. 0.25.0 wrote schema defaults into the export; 0.27.0 does not. So the exporter has already begun doing what BL-198 asks, while BL-198 itself is still listed PLANNED in epoch:planned-one-write-surface — worth reconciling. And the flip demonstrates the trap in the fix: suppressing defaults does not remove the disagreement, it MOVES it to the version transition. Both incidents happened in exactly such a window, so 'stop serializing defaults' makes the steady state clean and the upgrade moment worse unless the comparison also becomes version-aware.

WHAT THIS IS NOT: it is not evidence that export_graph loses design, and not evidence that its divergence guard is under-reporting. Both claims were made and both were wrong. The guard's message is accurate at node and edge granularity, and defaults were never design, so nothing was lost either time. Recorded here because the false claim is the measurement — what serialized defaults cost is precisely that two careful readers reached the same wrong conclusion from the same true output.

SEPARATELY TRUE AND NOT A DEFECT: reflow2_check reads artifact checksums and anchored gaps, never node properties, so it stayed green through both episodes. That means the CI gate and compare_designs answer different questions about whether the record matches the graph, which is worth knowing before either is relied on as the other.
